manifest.name: dsh-plugin-relay
manifest.description: DeepSeek Harness (dsh) plugin that routes model traffic through new-api-family relay panels (one-api / new-api / Veloera / done-hub / ...) — several panels at once, each its own model provider: manage panels (accordion with inline keys / models / dashboard / logs tabs), create / edit / delete and switch API keys, sync each key's model list with pricing, review usage dashboard (dual-axis) and logs, and configure model capabilities from a mainstream-model knowledge base — all from the dsh Plugins settings page

scripts.prepublishOnly: npm run typecheck && npm run build

bundle.text:
# The dsh-plugin-relay bundle patch.
#
# The only row here mounts the host plugin. Everything panel-specific — the
# per-panel pi-ai route profiles (baseURL, key reference, model catalog) and
# the default model — is written at runtime into the active profile's patch
# document (the `relay` and `llm-pi-ai` entries' config, hot-reloaded through
# the volatile schema fields) when a panel is added, a key is picked, or a
# capability is saved. dsh-base already mounts llm-pi-ai dormant with zero
# routes; each panel's route materializes on its first key use and follows
# the panel's connection settings from then on.
#
# The row carries no config: the entry's whole state is user-layer (the
# profile patch), editable per field without a restart (all Config fields are
# `.volatile()`). No defaults name any particular panel. The entry id `relay`
# doubles as the settings namespace the client page edits.

- insert:
    - id: relay
      name: dsh-plugin-relay

readme.text: A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`) plugin that connects dsh to any **new-api-family relay panel** (one-api / new-api / Veloera / done-hub / ...). Everything lives in dsh's **Plugins panel** — no CLI, no config files to hand-edit, and no panel-specific defaults baked in. Since v0.6.0 you can connect **several panels at once** — each one is its own model provider inside dsh, selectable side by side in the model picker.

- **Panels** — the *Connection* tab is an **accordion**: every connected panel is a collapsible row (account, balance, synced models, active key at a glance — the account line fills in lazily, so one unreachable panel never blocks the list), and expanding it folds the panel's four sub-tabs (API keys / models / dashboard / usage logs) inline; at most one panel is expanded at a time. New panels are added with *Add panel*: name (immutable after creation — it names the dsh model provider too), base URL, access token (write-only), and user ID — there is **no edit form**; changing a connection means delete + re-create. Each panel gets a **Test connection** button that classifies failures readably: unreachable network, invalid token, or user-ID mismatch. The delete dialog warns about capability overrides being removed and about dsh's default model pointing at the panel.
- **API keys** (per panel) — create, edit (name / group / quota / expiry / enable-disable), delete, and switch with one click on *Use*. Editing happens **in place** like the official Models page: the row expands into an editor card (one card at a time), *Apply* writes immediately and keeps the card open on failure, and del

| Connection (panel list) | API keys | Models |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |
| **Dashboard** | **Usage logs** | **Capabilities** |
|  |  |  |

Requires dsh ≥ 0.2.1-alpha.2, Node ≥ 20, and pnpm on PATH (dsh installs plugins through pnpm).

```sh

npm install && npm run build
dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-plugin-relay
```

Install into the `headless` profile the same way (`--profile headless`) if you use headless sessions. Then restart `dsh web` and open the **Plugins** panel → **Relay**.

1. Open **Settings → Relay → Connection**, press *Add panel*, and fill in a name (letters/digits/`_`/`-`, ≤32 chars — it becomes the model provider's name), the panel origin (no `/v1` suffix), the access token from the panel's personal page (client token / access token), and the user ID shown on the same page. *Test connection* verifies the trio before you commit to keys.
2. Click the panel's row to **expand it inline**. On **API keys**, create a key if you don't have one (or press *Use* on an existing one). The plugin writes the key into the dsh credential store, builds the panel's model route, and syncs the key's model catalog. Repeat for as many panels as you like — they all stay live side by side.
3. On **Models**, review pricing per model; refreshing keeps dsh's route catalog in step with what the key can actually call.
4. On **Dashboard** and **Usage logs**, keep an eye on balance and consumption; both read the panel's reporting APIs read-only.
5. On **Capabilities** (main page), browse the preset entries (searchable, collapsed by default) and copy any of them into *My entries* when you need a tweak; the presets fetch automatically from models.dev on first use (once a day aft

- The plugin's state is its composition entry's config (a `panels` dict with each panel's connection fields — the access token is a secret field redacted on the wire — plus the global knowledge base and per-panel override groups; all fields are hot-editable `.volatile()` fields of the profile patch), it serves `/api/relay/{state,panels,panels-create,panels-delete,account,connection-test,keys,keys-create,keys-update,keys-delete,use,models,capabilities,model-info,knowledge-refresh,dashboard,logs,logs-stat,logs-meta}` inside dsh's authenticated web fence.
- On first key switch per panel it writes the panel's pi-ai route profile (`api: openai-completions`, `baseURL: <panel>/v1`, `apiKeyEnv: RELAY_API_KEY_<PANEL>`, merged model catalog) into the `llm-pi-ai` entry's config — dsh hot-reloads routes, so no restart. The API key itself resolves per request from the panel's credential reference.
- Catalog sync merges by model id: manual edits of surviving ids are preserved; ids the key lost are removed, so dsh only offers models the key can call. Capability fields on the entries are **derived state**: each sync, each capability save, and each preset refresh replays the overrides → knowledge b

- Each panel's access token lives in a secret settings field (redacted on every wire surface, including nested inside the panels dict); API keys are written only to the server-side credential store (`.credentials.yaml`, 0600) and never returned to the browser — key creation responses are stripped server-side, and no "copy key" feature exists.
- All plugin routes sit inside dsh's browser trust fence (same origin + signed session); unauthenticated requests get 401.
- The models.dev lookup runs host-side (cached, single-flight); the browser never talks to third parties directly. The preset fetch never touches the relay panel and never introduces credentials.

- Requires dsh ≥ **0.2.1-alpha.2** (`engines.dsh` enforces it) — the first host line with the entry-config settings model this plugin's page and volatile hot writes build on. The host's frozen browser module table supplies `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives` (consumed as a stable-subset API; installed as a devDependency **pinned to the host-matching version** for types only) and the storage stack (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage` as a peer dependency — dsh-base mounts the hub and the json backend for every base-backed profile; on a profile without the stack the plugin degrades to a memory-only preset cache).
- The plugin deliberately sticks to the verified primitives subset (Button / Switch / Pill / Tag / StateDot / Menu / Modal) and re-runs a browser walkthrough whenever the dsh dev dependency is upgraded (see docs/PUBLISHING.md).

- Management-API calls need the paired user ID (typed once per panel; see the panel's personal page).
- Model capacity falls back to id-prefix heuristics when neither the panel nor the knowledge base reports a value; unknown ids fall back to 131072 context / 8192 output.
- Knowledge-base matching demands equality at every layer (case-fold, suffix strip, version-separator swap, variant completion) and gives up on ambiguity; channel-named panel-specific models (e.g. `grok-video`) match nothing by design.
- The preset only carries mainstream models — first-party providers released within the last year. Panels selling older or niche models fall back to unconfigured; add your own entries or hit *Refresh presets* (same rules).
- **First use needs one online fetch**: a fresh install (or a deleted storage file) shows no preset entries until the first models.dev fetch succeeds; the knowledge base, overrides, connections, and model sync all work regardless. Offline new installs stay in that state until the host can reach models.dev (respecting the host's proxy environment).
- Upgrading from ≤0.7.0: a stale `capabilityPresetDelta` key may linger in the profile patch. The new schema never decl

```sh
npm install        # @deepseek-ai/dsh is a devDependency; runtime has zero dependencies (schemastery + dsh-storage are peers)
npm run typecheck  # tsc --noEmit
npm run build      # tsdown → lib/index.js (host ESM) + lib/client.js (wrapped browser bundle)
npm test           # vitest: unit tests + mock relay panel, never touches a real dsh home
See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for release history, [docs/](docs) for development notes (worklog, specs, publishing checklist), and [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for dsh integration semantics.
